label: <DEL> step of longer sequences (plus the last original steps of length-9 sequences)
explanation: Fires mostly on the <DEL> input (87% of activation mass; rate 0.65 at the delimiter). The rate and mass at the delimiter go up with sequence length L, and the strongest activations (near max) are <DEL> steps of L=8-9 sequences. A weaker ramp shows up in the last few original-phase steps of long sequences (t>=7, rate 0.65 at orig_idx 8), climbing toward the <DEL>. Sequences whose first token is p, t or k fire more often and more strongly, so short sequences that start with them still fire at <DEL>, while many long sequences that start with digits or x/b/m stay silent. Almost never fires in the copy phase (1140 of 2.7M steps) or at t<3. Input token identity outside <DEL> has no effect.

issues: The core claims hold. Phase shares on dev are delimiter 0.868, original 0.132 and copy 0.000 (1140 steps). There are zero activations at t<3. Delimiter rate rises with L: L=5 0.33, L=6 0.56, L=9 0.997. The original predicate reproduces on test: P 0.812, R 0.759, F1 0.785, mass recall 0.892.

The first-token effect is a systematic gap that the original predicate ignores. At <DEL>, sequences whose first token is p, t or k fire far above the base rate for their length: L=4 precision 0.75, while all L<6 <DEL> steps together score 0.25; L=6 0.97 vs 0.52 for other first tokens. Test misses are dominated by short p/t/k sequences firing at <DEL> and by original-phase ramps at t=4-7 (e.g. 'p z t s w m z d' fires from t=5 on).

The explanation's claim that long sequences starting with digits or x/b/m stay silent is overstated. <DEL> at L=7 with a digit first token fires at a rate of 0.92, and with an x/b/m first token at 0.85.

The original-phase ramp follows absolute position t, not 'climbing toward the <DEL>' / 'last original steps'. At t=7, L=8 (the last original step) and L=9 (two steps before <DEL>) fire at the same rate, 0.271 each. The rate depends on t, not on distance to the delimiter. Calling it 'last original steps of length-9 sequences' is only true because t>=8 forces L=9.
There is also a smaller history effect: if the sequence contains an x, the L=6 <DEL> rate drops from 0.61 to 0.37. Many false positives are L=6-7 <DEL> steps of sequences that contain x.
F1 is 0.785, below 0.8. Adding the first_tok term pushes test F1 above 0.8 (0.811), so leaving it out leaves a known systematic class unexplained.
skeptic.revised_label: Position/length ramp peaking at <DEL>: fires at the delimiter of longer sequences (L>=6, plus shorter sequences starting with p/t/k) and in original-phase steps at absolute t>=7-8; boosted when the first token is p/t/k; silent in the copy phase
